questions.question: What is the identifying signal of runaway form one, "spinning in place"?
options: The request parameters between adjacent two turns are identical (difference of zero)
The model swaps a different wording each turn
questions.explanation: See the "Runaway form one: spinning in place" section: the identifying signal is that the request parameters between adjacent two turns differ by zero — step-inspection, if in place, should have raised an alarm at turn 3.

questions.question: How does runaway form two, "goal drift", work mechanically?
options: The model re-interprets the task every turn, and accumulated failures push it toward easier adjacent tasks
The model automatically switches to a different model
The context window is too small and evicts the task goal
Tool return values pollute the task goal
questions.explanation: See the "Runaway form two: goal drift" section: the loop's "goal" is only text inside the context; the model re-interprets the task every turn, and accumulated early failures push it toward easier adjacent tasks — that is the mechanism of drift.

questions.question: What stopping mechanism finally ended the experiment's "12 turns of spinning, 7% completion"?
options: A manually re-enabled circuit breaker (dual condition: ≥10 consecutive failures or cost above ¥0.5)
The model itself producing a final answer
questions.explanation: See the "The guardrail family and the post-mortem" section: the manually re-enabled circuit breaker in the demo fired under a dual condition — ≥10 consecutive failures or cost above ¥0.5 — either is enough to trigger; in the experiment the cost threshold fired first.
